statement: The repository and service are named chat-orchestrator.
criterion: The repository and the deployed service name are both chat-orchestrator.

statement: The service is implemented in Go, with PostgreSQL as the durable adapter.
criterion: The source is Go and the durable store adapter targets PostgreSQL.

statement: The service runs as a single active writer and exposes a synchronous, non-streaming HTTP API.
criterion: Only one writer process is active at a time, and no endpoint streams a response.

statement: The service maintains durable conversations that combine an external Knowledge Base, a replaceable Decision Model and a replaceable LLM.
criterion: A turn retrieves from the KB, takes a typed decision and generates through the LLM, and swapping the Decision Model or LLM adapter changes no core code.

statement: A client can resume a stored session after a disconnect or a process restart.
criterion: After the client disconnects or the service restarts, the session and its committed turns can still be read and continued.

statement: By default the service admits at most 100 active turns, keeps order within each session and bounds waiting work.
criterion: At most 100 active turns at default configuration; same-session turns complete in admission order; the wait queue has a fixed bound.

statement: The service reduces avoidable token consumption through context management, incremental summaries, idempotency and provider-native caching.
criterion: Tests show bounded context, reuse of summaries, no repeated paid calls on idempotent replay, and cache directives on supported adapters.

statement: The capitalized keywords MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are interpreted per BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174).
criterion: Every normative keyword is read per BCP 14 only when capitalized.

statement: Every normative requirement ID stays traceable to implementation or configuration evidence and named acceptance tests.
criterion: A traceability record maps each requirement ID to evidence and at least one named test.

statement: Any departure from a SHOULD requirement has a recorded rationale and matching test expectations.
criterion: Each SHOULD departure has a written rationale and a test expectation.

statement: The service owns the conversation API, state semantics, orchestration, scheduling and idempotency.
criterion: These concerns are implemented within the service, not delegated to an external product.

statement: Durable persistence uses PostgreSQL as the pilot adapter behind application-owned persistence contracts.
criterion: The core depends only on persistence interfaces, and the PostgreSQL adapter implements them.

statement: Knowledge retrieval uses the existing external KB; the service supplies only the outbound adapter and protocol mapping.
criterion: No retrieval engine is built; the KB adapter maps the approved wire contract.

statement: Typed decisions use TypeSafe AI Jev as the first adapter behind a normalized contract that another provider can implement.
criterion: The Jev adapter implements the normalized decision contract, and a test double implements the same contract.

statement: Generation and summarization use an application-owned LLM contract with Anthropic Messages and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions adapters.
criterion: Both protocol adapters implement the same LLM contract.

statement: Each applicable LLM adapter implements and tests provider-native prompt caching.
criterion: Adapter tests show the provider cache directives being sent and cache usage being parsed.

statement: A generic KB or infrastructure cache is optional and sits behind a replaceable adapter; Redis is not required.
criterion: The service runs with no cache and no Redis.

statement: Identity issuance and model hosting are external dependencies, not products of this project.
criterion: The project contains no identity provider and no model-hosting component.

statement: The core workflow depends on application-owned capability types, not database or AI-provider wire types.
criterion: Core packages import no database driver and no provider SDK or wire type.

statement: The service ships a working PostgreSQL adapter, a KB outbound adapter, a Jev adapter and both selected LLM protocol adapters.
criterion: Each adapter is present, configured and passes its conformance tests.

statement: A selected remote persistence, summary or cache integration provides a real configured outbound client with a versioned protocol and conformance tests.
criterion: Each selected remote integration has a configured client, a protocol version and conformance tests, not only a Go interface.

statement: The pilot introduces no external KB, model training or hosting platform, identity provider, UI, distributed work queue or extra microservice.
criterion: The delivered system contains none of the listed components.

statement: Streaming, WebSockets, async job delivery, automatic provider failover, autonomous tools, full-response or semantic caching and multi-writer scheduling are out of scope.
criterion: None of the deferred features is implemented.

statement: The service guards against an accidental second process but does not need to support multiple active writers.
criterion: A second process cannot become an active writer.

statement: At the default configuration at most 100 turns are active, and at most one per session.
criterion: Active turns never exceed 100 globally or 1 per session.

statement: A logical request commits at most one user/assistant pair and one conversation-version increment.
criterion: Under retries and duplicates, each logical request adds at most one pair and one version increment.

statement: A successful chat response is sent only after its complete conversational outcome is durably committed.
criterion: No 200 chat response precedes the durable commit of its outcome.

statement: The next turn in a session loads the latest committed state after its predecessor's outcome is resolved.
criterion: A turn's context includes the preceding committed turn of the same session.

statement: Failed, cancelled or uncertain attempts never appear as completed turns in the transcript.
criterion: The transcript holds only completed turns.

statement: Cache state, provider conversation handles and process memory are never the authoritative record of a conversation.
criterion: With caches cleared and the process restarted, the conversation is fully restored from the durable store.

statement: The persistent deployment uses PostgreSQL with versioned migrations, a pinned database and toolchain profile and a documented backup and restore procedure.
criterion: Migrations are versioned, versions are pinned, and the backup and restore procedure is documented and tested.

statement: An in-memory store is limited to tests or labelled synthetic development mode and never satisfies durable-persistence acceptance.
criterion: The in-memory store is unavailable outside tests or labelled dev mode, and durability tests run against PostgreSQL.

statement: Deployment uses one intended replica with a non-overlapping replacement strategy, such as Recreate, in addition to the runtime writer guard.
criterion: The deployment manifest declares one replica and a non-overlapping strategy.

statement: Outside synthetic dev mode, the service validates a bearer token's signature, algorithm allowlist, issuer, audience, expiry and not-before before touching a session or request record.
criterion: Tokens failing any one check are rejected before any session or request access.

statement: The pilot JWT profile uses RS256 with a configured trusted key or JWKS source and normalizes claims into an application-owned principal.
criterion: Non-RS256 tokens are rejected, and the principal is built from the claims.

statement: The iss, aud, exp and iat claims, and nbf where present, are validated as issuer, audience and validity interval.
criterion: A token with a wrong issuer or audience, or outside its validity, is rejected.

statement: The tenant_id claim is a non-empty tenant identifier.
criterion: tenant_id is non-empty and at most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

statement: The sub claim is a non-empty subject identifier.
criterion: sub is non-empty and at most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

statement: The roles claim holds only allowlisted role strings.
criterion: At most 32 roles, each at most 64 bytes.

statement: The authz_version claim is an optional trusted authorization revision, required where revision-based revocation is claimed.
criterion: A deployment claiming revision-based revocation rejects tokens without authz_version.

statement: The normalized principal is {tenant_id, subject, roles, authz_version}.
criterion: The principal type has exactly those four fields.

statement: Session ownership derives from (tenant_id, subject), and client JSON or untrusted headers cannot override owner, tenant or role.
criterion: Override attempts in the body or headers have no effect on ownership.

statement: Unknown, deleted and other-owner resources return the same 404 after authentication, with no existence oracle.
criterion: The three cases return byte-identical 404 responses.

statement: Retrieval permissions derive server-side from trusted roles and authorization scope, not from the session identifier.
criterion: Retrieval scope changes with the roles, not with the session ID.

statement: The service re-evaluates its trusted authorization snapshot before starting queued work and before returning history, status or a replay.
criterion: Revoked authorization blocks queued work and blocks history, status and replay reads.

statement: A token that expires while its request is queued yields an authentication failure before paid work; a renewed token allows a same-key retry only where the idempotency rules permit.
criterion: An expired queued request fails authentication with no paid call.

statement: Token validity at request start is not an indefinite authorization grant.
criterion: Authorization is rechecked at later stages.

statement: Offline authentication tests use local signing keys and a local trusted-key fixture, with no network identity discovery.
criterion: The auth tests pass without network access.

statement: An incompatible existing gateway needs an explicit verified claim mapping, and the core principal model never changes silently.
criterion: Any gateway mapping is explicit and tested.

statement: The service implements the endpoint contract as synchronous, non-streaming HTTP/JSON with a published OpenAPI specification.
criterion: An OpenAPI document is published, and the endpoints conform to it.

statement: POST /v1/sessions creates an empty owned session with a server-generated ID and conversation version 0.
criterion: Returns 201 with a new ID and version 0.

statement: POST /v1/chat returns 200 only for a committed answer, ask_clarification or cannot_answer outcome.
criterion: No 200 without a committed outcome of one of the three actions.

statement: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id} returns the authorized metadata, locale, retrieval scope and conversation version.
criterion: Returns 200 with those fields to the owner.

statement: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/messages returns bounded, cursor-paginated committed messages in ascending sequence.
criterion: Returns 200 with a bounded page in ascending sequence and a cursor.

statement: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/requests/{request_id} returns the known request state and stored result or problem.
criterion: Returns 200 with the state, and 404 when the request is unknown or inaccessible.

statement: DELETE /v1/sessions/{session_id} purges live application content.
criterion: Returns 204 after the purge, and 409 if the session is busy.

statement: GET /health/live reports process liveness without paid dependency calls.
criterion: Liveness responds and makes no KB or model call.

statement: GET /health/ready reports whether configuration, storage, writer ownership and startup recovery permit admission.
criterion: Readiness fails while any of these is not satisfied.

statement: POST /v1/chat rejects an unknown session with 404 and never creates one implicitly.
criterion: Chat on an unknown session returns 404, and no session is created.

statement: Session creation accepts only the allowlisted locale, metadata and retrieval fields.
criterion: Any other field is rejected.

statement: The session-creation body takes the illustrated shape: locale, metadata (product_id, product_version) and retrieval (corpus_ids, filters).
criterion: The example body is accepted.

statement: The metadata and filter allowlist is product_id and product_version, each a bounded string.
criterion: Each value is a string of at most 128 bytes.

statement: Session creation accepts a bounded list of corpus IDs.
criterion: Up to 8 corpus IDs, each at most 128 bytes.

statement: Empty metadata and empty filters are valid.
criterion: A session with empty metadata and filters is created.

statement: Unknown fields in session creation are rejected.
criterion: An unknown field yields 400.

statement: Metadata and filters are query hints, not verified user facts or permission grants.
criterion: Supplying a filter grants no extra retrieval permission.

statement: Client retrieval preferences only narrow the server-authorized scope, and an unauthorized corpus or filter is rejected with 403 RETRIEVAL_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN.
criterion: An unauthorized corpus or filter returns 403 RETRIEVAL_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN.

statement: Session locale and retrieval preferences are immutable in the pilot; a chat request may override only its response locale.
criterion: No endpoint changes a session's locale or retrieval settings.

statement: The chat request body takes the illustrated shape: request_id, session_id, question and locale.
criterion: The example body is accepted.

statement: Every chat request contains non-empty request_id, session_id and question fields.
criterion: A missing or empty field yields 400.

statement: Request parsing enforces size limits and strict JSON and schema validation before admission.
criterion: 32 KiB body, 8 KiB UTF-8 question, 128-byte request ID.

statement: Request IDs use ASCII letters, digits, hyphen and underscore, and session IDs use the service UUID format.
criterion: Other characters or formats yield 400.

statement: Empty or whitespace-only questions, duplicate JSON keys, trailing JSON values, unknown properties and invalid UTF-8 are invalid.
criterion: Each case yields 400.

statement: Oversized bodies return 413, and field or schema violations return 400.
criterion: An oversized body returns 413, and a schema violation returns 400.

statement: Lower configured limits need matching published schemas.
criterion: The OpenAPI schema reflects any lowered limit.

statement: History pagination is bounded, uses session-bound opaque cursors and is stable under concurrent append.
criterion: Default page 50, max page 100; ascending order is stable under concurrent append.

statement: API responses expose only application-owned fields and bounded chat bodies, with no raw upstream errors, credentials or prompts.
criterion: Chat response body at most 64 KiB, with no leaked upstream or internal content.

statement: A committed response conforms to the normalized envelope and the outcome table.
criterion: Every committed response validates against the envelope schema.

statement: The response envelope carries request_id, session_id, session_version, action, reason_code, locale, answer, sources and message_refs.
criterion: The example envelope validates.

statement: answer/grounded has a non-empty answer, at least one valid KB citation and sources equal to the cited KB subset.
criterion: Each grounded answer cites at least one source, and its sources equal the cited set.

statement: answer/conversation_meta answers about the transcript with sources=[] and supporting message sequences in message_refs.
criterion: sources is empty, and message_refs lists authorized sequences.

statement: answer/smalltalk is a bounded, localized acknowledgement with both reference arrays empty.
criterion: Both arrays are empty.

statement: ask_clarification outcomes carry a non-empty localized clarification with empty reference arrays and no unsupported factual answer.
criterion: The clarification text is non-empty, and both arrays are empty.

statement: cannot_answer for no_evidence, conflicting, insufficient or uncertain carries a non-empty localized explanation with empty reference arrays.
criterion: The explanation is non-empty, and both arrays are empty.

statement: cannot_answer for out_of_scope, history_unavailable or provider_refusal carries a non-empty controlled explanation with empty reference arrays.
criterion: The explanation is non-empty, and both arrays are empty.

statement: All three actions are successful outcomes and increment the conversation version.
criterion: Each action commits and increments the version by 1.

statement: Infrastructure errors neither count as successful outcomes nor increment the version.
criterion: After an infrastructure error, the version is unchanged.

statement: Source titles, URIs and revisions are optional when the KB does not supply them, and absent values are never invented.
criterion: Missing KB fields stay absent in the sources.

statement: message_refs refers to transcript sequence numbers in the same session only.
criterion: No message_ref points to another session.

statement: The response locale resolves as request override, then session locale, then the default tr-TR, with tr-TR and en-US supported.
criterion: Each precedence level is honored in a test.

statement: Response language follows the explicit locale contract, not a language detector.
criterion: The output language matches the resolved locale.

statement: A Turkish request with tr-TR stays Turkish when the evidence is English.
criterion: A tr-TR request over English evidence gets a Turkish response.

statement: Unsupported locales return 400.
criterion: An unsupported locale yields 400.

statement: Source titles need not be translated.
criterion: Titles are passed through untranslated.

statement: The store retains sessions, committed messages, request journals, provider-call journals, summary checkpoints and provenance enough to enforce the data contract.
criterion: The schema holds every entity in the data contract.

statement: A session records ID, owner, locale, retrieval settings, authorization fingerprint, conversation version, lifecycle state and retention timestamps.
criterion: The session record holds each listed field.

statement: A committed message records session ID, increasing sequence, role, text, logical request, references and creation time.
criterion: The message record holds each listed field, with strictly increasing sequence.

statement: A request journal records logical key, fingerprint version and hash, admitted and execution versions, attempt sequence, owner epoch, state and saved result or problem.
criterion: The request-journal record holds each listed field.

statement: A provider-call journal records a unique call ID, stage, input hash, model and config versions, dispatch intent, outcome, reusable result and usage state.
criterion: The provider-call record holds each listed field, with a unique call ID.

statement: A summary checkpoint records session ID, covered_seq, optional partial cursor, summary_version, bounded summary, source hash, procedure versions and writer epoch.
criterion: The checkpoint record holds each listed field.

statement: A reserved ID registry keeps non-reusable session-ID digests and their lifecycle status, separate from conversation content.
criterion: A deleted session ID cannot be reused, and the registry holds no content.

statement: A committed turn remains available after the service stops and restarts against the same store.
criterion: After a restart, the committed turns are readable.

statement: Finalization atomically writes the user/assistant pair, source references, new version and completed idempotency result.
criterion: A failure injected mid-finalization leaves none or all of them written.

statement: Finalization checks expected version, logical-request uniqueness, live session status and current writer epoch in the same transaction.
criterion: Each failed check aborts the commit.

statement: No session or database transaction lock is held across a KB or model network call.
criterion: No transaction is open during an outbound call.

statement: A lost database-commit acknowledgement triggers authoritative result reconciliation before any inference is repeated.
criterion: A simulated lost acknowledgement leads to reconciliation with no repeated paid call.

statement: A committed result wins over an expired HTTP connection.
criterion: A commit after the client disconnect stays committed and replayable.

statement: An unconfirmed commit is not treated as proof of rollback.
criterion: An unconfirmed commit is reconciled, not assumed rolled back.

statement: While the store is unreachable, status stays explicitly unavailable or pending reconciliation, never an invented result.
criterion: During a store outage, status reports unavailable or pending.

statement: Original transcript messages stay accessible independently of summaries until deletion or retention removes them.
criterion: Messages remain readable after summarization.

statement: The PostgreSQL implementation passes real-store conformance, migration, restart, atomicity and backup and restore tests.
criterion: Each of those suites passes against real PostgreSQL.

statement: A valid summary checkpoint commits independently of the current chat turn without incrementing the conversation version.
criterion: A checkpoint commit leaves the version unchanged.

statement: Checkpoint updates use coverage and version compare-and-swap plus writer and lifecycle fencing.
criterion: A checkpoint never covers uncommitted turns and never survives deletion.

statement: Checkpoints are derived data; they do not replace transcript authority or prove the current message was answered.
criterion: The transcript, not the checkpoint, is authoritative.

statement: The idempotency key is (tenant_id, subject, session_id, request_id), with authentication and ownership checks before lookup or replay.
criterion: The same request_id under a different owner is a distinct key, and unauthenticated replay is refused.

statement: A repeated key with a different semantic-input fingerprint returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and leaves the existing request unchanged.
criterion: A changed question under the same key returns 409, and the stored request is unchanged.

statement: The fingerprint covers the exact accepted question, resolved locale and immutable retrieval and session configuration identity.
criterion: Changing any of these changes the fingerprint.

statement: The fingerprint excludes transport timestamps, trace IDs and renewed token bytes.
criterion: Changing any of these leaves the fingerprint unchanged.

statement: Security-policy changes are handled by authorization checks, not by the fingerprint.
criterion: A role change does not cause IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

statement: The service claims a logical request atomically before execution and resolves concurrent duplicates without a check-then-insert race.
criterion: Concurrent duplicates produce exactly one execution.

statement: Pre-admission validation and overload rejections create no durable in-progress request or completed turn.
criterion: After a 400 or 429, no request or turn record exists.

statement: Completed request keys and response bodies stay replayable for the retained session lifetime, subject to authorization and deletion.
criterion: A completed key replays its saved body while the session is retained.

statement: A first attempt may wait behind earlier same-session work and binds its execution version to the state it actually reads.
criterion: The execution version equals the version read at start.

statement: The admission-time version is not an execution precondition for a first attempt.
criterion: A first attempt that waited still executes after the version changes.

statement: A retryable request re-enters the queue with a new admission sequence and passes its retry-version guard when execution starts.
criterion: The guard is checked at start, not at re-enqueue.

statement: The retry-version guard equals the execution version if execution began, or the admission-time version otherwise.
criterion: The guard value matches the rule in both cases.

statement: If the guard differs from the current version at retry execution, the service returns and retains 409 STATE_CONFLICT without a paid call.
criterion: A retry after another commit returns 409 STATE_CONFLICT, with no paid call.

statement: An earlier attempt cannot silently retry against a newer context after a later turn commits.
criterion: An A1 retry after A2 commits is refused.

statement: Request status and same-key resubmission implement the complete state table.
criterion: Each state's resubmission behavior is tested.

statement: A queued request resubmitted returns 409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS with a bounded Retry-After and no duplicate waiter.
criterion: One waiter only; 409 with Retry-After.

statement: A running request resubmitted returns 409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS without a second execution.
criterion: One execution only.

statement: A committing request resubmitted returns 409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS with status or reconciliation guidance.
criterion: 409 with guidance.

statement: A completed request resubmitted returns 200 with the saved response and Idempotent-Replayed: true, with no new external calls.
criterion: 200 replay, header set, zero outbound calls.

statement: A retryable request resubmitted is re-admitted under the same key or rejected for overload, auth or version conflict, never duplicating a committed turn.
criterion: No duplicate turn.

statement: An uncertain request resubmitted returns 409 OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN with no automatic new attempt.
criterion: 409 OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN, no new attempt.

statement: A failed_final request resubmitted replays its saved status or problem with Idempotent-Replayed: true.
criterion: The saved problem is replayed, with the header set.

statement: GET .../requests/{request_id} returns a status envelope with state, attempt, timestamps, result or problem and next_action.
criterion: The envelope has those fields, with next_action one of wait, retry_same_id, use_new_id or none.

statement: A disconnect, queue deadline or shutdown before any unresolved chargeable dispatch produces retryable, not a permanent cancelled state.
criterion: Such a request ends in retryable.

statement: A cancellation or deadline after a possibly accepted call with no recoverable result produces uncertain once reconciliation fails.
criterion: Such a request ends in uncertain.

statement: A paid call with a durably saved usable result is not uncertain merely because money was spent.
criterion: That request is not marked uncertain.

statement: A read-only KB may be billable; its configured effect and billing class decides whether an unanswered dispatch is uncertain.
criterion: A KB configured as billable leads to uncertain on an unanswered dispatch.

statement: Unknown billing semantics are treated conservatively.
criterion: An unknown billing class is treated as chargeable.

statement: Before each potentially chargeable dispatch, the service durably records a unique call ID, stage and input identity, writer epoch and dispatch_intent marker.
criterion: A marker row exists before every chargeable call.

statement: The service does not send a call when its dispatch marker cannot be written or writer ownership cannot be established.
criterion: With the marker write failing, no call is sent.

statement: A dispatch marker means "may have been sent," not "definitely received."
criterion: Marked calls without an outcome are treated as possibly sent.

statement: Each provider result is journaled as a known success, a verified rejection, a known unusable result or an unresolved outcome before any retry decision.
criterion: Every call has one of the four outcomes journaled before a retry.

statement: Saved stage outputs are reused only when input, model and policy, evidence snapshot, authorization and version identities all match.
criterion: A mismatch in any identity prevents reuse.

statement: A metadata-only log of a successful call is not a reusable result.
criterion: A call without a saved output is not reused.

statement: Reissuing a successful paid call whose result was not saved is not classified as a free retry.
criterion: Such a reissue is journaled as a possible duplicate charge.

statement: Known unusable output is a final protocol or generation error, not an unknown outcome.
criterion: Unusable output yields failed_final, not uncertain.

statement: Application and SDK retry layers share one bounded retry policy so nested retries cannot multiply paid requests.
criterion: Total paid attempts never exceed the single policy bound.

statement: max_uncertain_model_retries accepts only 0 or 1 and defaults to 0.
criterion: Allowed values {0,1}; default 0.

statement: An opted-in uncertain-model retry happens only within the connected original attempt, with unchanged input, valid ownership, enough budget and a journaled possible duplicate charge.
criterion: A retry outside any of these conditions is refused.

statement: Cancellation, restart, a changed model or policy and a new HTTP resubmission never authorize the optional uncertain retry.
criterion: Each of these cases yields no retry.

statement: The optional retry is not automatic provider failover.
criterion: The retry uses the same provider.

statement: Provider idempotency or reconciliation is used only where documented; unsupported TypeSafe behavior is never assumed.
criterion: There is no reliance on undocumented Jev idempotency.

statement: Request state transitions are constrained to queued, running, committing, completed, with exits to retryable, uncertain or failed_final and guarded retryable-to-queued.
criterion: Any other transition is rejected.

statement: Commit reconciliation resolves committing to completed, safe retryable or uncertain according to stored evidence.
criterion: Each resolution follows the evidence.

statement: A known aborted commit with a saved valid response can be retried without regeneration.
criterion: The retry commits the saved response with no model call.

statement: completed is immutable, and failed_final requires a new request ID.
criterion: A completed record never changes; a failed_final key is never re-executed.

statement: Clients do not re-enqueue uncertain under the same key.
criterion: A same-key resubmission of uncertain is refused.

statement: Late reconciliation may find a committed result or recover stage data, which becomes guarded retryable only if the original version still matches.
criterion: Recovered data with a stale version is not made retryable.

statement: Reconciliation cannot append an old turn after a later version committed.
criterion: No stale turn is appended.

statement: Startup recovery inspects abandoned records only after exclusive writer ownership is acquired and never replays the old in-memory queue.
criterion: Recovery waits for the lock and performs no queue replay.

statement: Recovery resolves committed records first, marks never-dispatched work retryable and unreconciled dispatches uncertain before sessions accept new work.
criterion: After recovery, every abandoned record has one of these states before admission.

statement: After a transport error, clients inspect request status, wait on active states, use saved results, retry the same ID if retryable and use a new ID only after accepting the consequences.
criterion: The documented client recovery flow matches the next_action values.

statement: A status 404 for the same authorized live session means no claim is known and permits resubmission with the original ID.
criterion: A resubmission after the 404 is accepted.

statement: A temporary 503 does not mean the request is absent.
criterion: A 503 status is not reported as unknown.

statement: Cancellation before finalization starts no detached turn commit; recoverable outputs allow only a guarded client retry.
criterion: After cancellation, no background commit occurs.

statement: At most one durable turn per logical key is guaranteed; exactly one provider charge is not promised.
criterion: No key ever has two turns.

statement: Before recovery or mutations, each process acquires a service-scoped PostgreSQL session advisory lock on a dedicated connection.
criterion: Recovery and admission start only after the lock is held.

statement: A process that cannot acquire the lock stays unready and never recovers, admits or dispatches.
criterion: A second process stays unready and does no work.

statement: The advisory lock is not a TTL lease.
criterion: Ownership does not expire on a timer.

statement: The lock connection is dedicated, not borrowed from the pool per operation.
criterion: The lock is held on a single dedicated connection.

statement: After obtaining the lock, the process allocates a monotonically increasing instance_epoch and publishes it in a durable writer-control row before recovery.
criterion: Each start gets a higher epoch, recorded before recovery.

statement: Every mutation, marker write and final commit enforces the current epoch transactionally, without a check-then-write race.
criterion: A stale-epoch write is rejected.

statement: Short transactions complete before takeover or are rejected as stale, never passing a detached epoch check.
criterion: No stale-epoch transaction commits after takeover.

statement: Request claims and stage journals carry their owning epoch, and recovery leaves records of a verified current owner untouched.
criterion: Recovery never alters current-owner records.

statement: Loss of the ownership connection fails readiness, stops admission and dispatch and cancels local work without reconnecting as the same owner.
criterion: After a lock-connection drop, readiness fails and no new call is sent.

statement: A replacement process passes the second-process and stale-writer acceptance tests before single-writer safety is claimed.
criterion: Both acceptance tests pass.

statement: Writer fencing cannot retract a call already accepted by a provider or fence an API without fencing support.
criterion: No such guarantee is claimed.

statement: Calls in flight during ownership loss stay under the uncertainty boundary; no distributed exactly-once claim is made.
criterion: Such calls are marked uncertain if not reconciled.

statement: With non-throttling dependencies, the scheduler runs 100 distinct sessions concurrently and never a 101st active turn.
criterion: Exactly 100 concurrently active; 101st never active.

statement: Same-session FIFO uses the server admission sequence, not client clocks or send order.
criterion: Order follows the admission sequence.

statement: Only the oldest waiting request of an idle session whose principal has quota is eligible for an active slot.
criterion: No other request takes a slot.

statement: Eligible sessions are selected FIFO, and a session's next request goes to the tail after its preceding turn resolves.
criterion: Session selection order is FIFO.

statement: Waiting work for a busy session or exhausted principal does not reserve global capacity or block other eligible sessions.
criterion: Other sessions proceed while such work waits.

statement: Initial admission limits are set.
criterion: 100 active globally, 100 waiting globally, 2 waiting per session, 10 active and 10 waiting per principal.

statement: All pre-execution waiting, including same-session waits, counts toward queue capacity and queue time.
criterion: Same-session waiters count against the caps and the timer.

statement: Principal quotas stop one subject from consuming the service through many sessions; tenant-wide fairness is not guaranteed.
criterion: One principal cannot exceed 10 active turns.

statement: Admission enforces global, session and principal limits atomically with bounded temporary reservations and durable claiming.
criterion: Concurrent admissions never exceed any limit.

statement: Session creation is rate-limited and capped per principal.
criterion: 30 creations/min, burst 10; at most 1,000 retained sessions per principal.

statement: Admission rejects with 429 and Retry-After when capacity is full or the estimated start delay exceeds the remaining budget.
criterion: 429 with Retry-After in both cases.

statement: The start-delay estimate is versioned and covers active residual work, earlier eligible work, same-session predecessors, quotas and observed throttling.
criterion: The estimator accounts for each listed input.

statement: Cold-start estimated turn duration is conservative and updated from observed durations.
criterion: Initial estimate 30 s.

statement: The 100-waiter cap leaves headroom against the 60-second wait budget under a 100-worker, 30-second-turn estimate.
criterion: About 200 starts possible in 60 s versus 100 waiters.

statement: Queue time, including same-session waits, is capped independently of the total attempt deadline.
criterion: Queue time max 60 s; total attempt deadline 180 s.

statement: The scheduler removes cancelled or expired waiters without downstream work or leaked reservations.
criterion: After expiry, no outbound call is made and the reservation counts return to their prior values.

statement: A start-budget guard refuses to start a turn with too little processing budget left after reserving finalization time.
criterion: Start refused when less than 60 s of processing budget remains.

statement: The per-session cap of two is an upper bound, not a promise to accept both when the predicted wait is too long.
criterion: A second waiter may be refused with 429.

statement: Admission handlers, goroutines, queue records and idle coordination objects are bounded and cleaned up without busy-waiting or ordering races.
criterion: After load and idle, goroutine and record counts return to baseline, with no busy-wait loop.

statement: The domain path runs: authenticate and validate, claim and schedule, bind version, prepare history, classify intent, retrieve evidence, assess evidence, generate when allowed, validate, commit atomically.
criterion: A traced domain turn runs these stages in this order.

statement: All inference shares the journaling, budget and cancellation rules.
criterion: Every model call is journaled, budgeted and cancellable.

statement: The KB capability accepts the original question, resolved query, bounded context, allowed corpus and filter scope, locale and optional document hints.
criterion: The KnowledgeQuery passed to the adapter carries each field.

statement: A follow-up query keeps the relevant referent from committed context, not just an isolated pronoun question.
criterion: A pronoun follow-up's resolved query names the earlier referent.

statement: The default query preparer is deterministic, combining the question with relevant product and session facts and recent user references.
criterion: The same inputs give the same resolved query.

statement: Previously cited document IDs are only boost hints, never mandatory filters.
criterion: Newer evidence outside the cited documents can still be retrieved.

statement: Extra LLM query rewriting is optional and explicitly charged and journaled.
criterion: When enabled, each rewrite call has a usage record.

statement: Query preparation preserves the user's question and distinguishes original text from resolved or translated query.
criterion: The query has separate question and resolved_query fields, and the question is unchanged.

statement: The KB adapter normalizes a bounded result into evidence items with text, document ID, chunk ID and available revision, title and reference metadata.
criterion: The normalized items carry those fields.

statement: Retrieval caps the evidence count and enforces byte and token budgets before inference.
criterion: At most 8 evidence items; configured byte and token budgets enforced.

statement: The KB adapter distinguishes an empty success, a transport or timeout failure, an access failure and malformed or oversized evidence.
criterion: Each case maps to a distinct result.

statement: KB failure never silently activates a general-knowledge answer path.
criterion: A KB failure yields an error, with no generation call.

statement: The KB wire protocol, auth, authorization propagation, filters, versioning, limits and error mapping are approved and frozen before their tests count as Gate A evidence.
criterion: A frozen, approved KB contract exists before Gate A.

statement: The application-owned KnowledgeQuery and KnowledgeResult shape is the mapping target, not a claim about the existing KB's fields or URL.
criterion: The adapter maps between the KB wire format and these types.

statement: KnowledgeQuery and KnowledgeResult have the stated fields.
criterion: The types define exactly the listed fields.

statement: The approved wire contract supplies the actual HTTP method, path, credentials and field mapping.
criterion: The adapter's configuration comes from the approved contract.

statement: No fabricated /query endpoint substitutes for the approved contract.
criterion: The adapter has no guessed endpoint.

statement: If the KB cannot enforce the access scope, a verified integration boundary is needed before real data is used; model filtering is not authorization.
criterion: Real data is used only behind an enforcing boundary.

statement: User content, KB passages and summaries stay untrusted and cannot change credentials, endpoints, roles, policy, actions or system instructions.
criterion: Prompt-injection tests change none of these.

statement: Conversation facts explain intent without replacing current KB evidence for fresh domain assertions.
criterion: A domain answer cites KB evidence, not the transcript.

statement: The pilot never fetches user-supplied URLs or executes model-selected tools.
criterion: A URL in the question is never fetched, and no tool is called.

statement: The first Decision Model adapter implements TypeSafe AI Jev through the pinned, tested POST /v1/systemone contract.
criterion: The adapter calls /v1/systemone and passes the contract tests.

statement: Every decision input includes the bounded conversational information needed to interpret the question, not only the last sentence.
criterion: The DecisionState includes the summary and recent turns.

statement: DecisionState has the stated fields: question, resolved query, locale, conversation, evidence, application scope and policy version.
criterion: The type defines those fields.

statement: Evidence is not_requested for intent classification and success (possibly empty) for post-retrieval assessment.
criterion: The retrieval_status value matches the stage.

statement: Credentials, raw identity tokens and unnecessary personal identifiers are never model input.
criterion: Captured model inputs contain none of them.

statement: The resolved query used for retrieval is included in the evidence-assessment state.
criterion: The assessment input's resolved_query equals the retrieval query.

statement: The service classifies intent as domain, conversation_meta, smalltalk or out_of_scope before domain retrieval.
criterion: The classification precedes any KB call.

statement: Ambiguous intent produces ask_clarification / intent_ambiguous without guessing a domain workflow.
criterion: An ambiguous classification commits intent_ambiguous with no KB call.

statement: The default intent-confidence policy accepts a classification only when it is clear enough.
criterion: Top probability >= 0.70 and margin over the second >= 0.20.

statement: A domain request with successful retrieval gets three independent assessments: needs_clarification, evidence_sufficient and evidence_conflicting.
criterion: All three judgments are recorded per domain turn.

statement: Jev uses one batched evaluation of three atomic Noul questions over the complete shared state.
criterion: One Jev call returns all three judgments.

statement: The assessment contract distinguishes yes, no and uncertain for each judgment and keeps raw probability separately.
criterion: Each judgment has a verdict and its raw probability.

statement: needs_clarification and evidence_conflicting map probabilities to verdicts by fixed thresholds.
criterion: p <= 0.20 no; p >= 0.80 yes; otherwise uncertain.

statement: evidence_sufficient maps probabilities to verdicts by fixed thresholds.
criterion: p <= 0.20 no; p >= 0.85 yes; otherwise uncertain.

statement: Threshold boundaries are inclusive.
criterion: p = 0.20 maps to no, and p = 0.80 (0.85) maps to yes.

statement: Thresholds, question text, normalization rules and action precedence are versioned together in a provider and model-specific policy profile.
criterion: A single policy version identifies all of them.

statement: The domain workflow applies the first-match policy table after authentication, budget and reconciliation checks.
criterion: Each policy row is exercised, and the first match wins.

statement: A KB transport, access or protocol error yields no turn and a mapped 502, 503 or 504, with retry classification by side-effect evidence.
criterion: No turn is committed, and the status is mapped.

statement: A decision transport error, invalid or missing assessment or unsupported result yields no turn and a mapped error or 502 DECISION_INVALID, with no generation fallback.
criterion: No turn and no generation call.

statement: needs_clarification=yes commits ask_clarification / needs_clarification.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: needs_clarification=uncertain commits ask_clarification / clarification_uncertain.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: Successful retrieval with zero items commits cannot_answer / no_evidence.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: evidence_conflicting=yes commits cannot_answer / conflicting.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: evidence_conflicting=uncertain commits cannot_answer / uncertain.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: evidence_sufficient=no commits cannot_answer / insufficient.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: evidence_sufficient=uncertain commits cannot_answer / uncertain.
criterion: That outcome is committed.

statement: Clarification no, conflict no, sufficiency yes and non-empty evidence lead to generating and validating answer / grounded.
criterion: Only this combination calls generation.

statement: Contradictory assessments resolve uniquely: clarification precedes missing or conflicting evidence, and conflict precedes sufficiency.
criterion: Contradictory inputs yield the higher-precedence outcome.

statement: Uncertain is derived from the normalized assessment, not asked as a fourth class.
criterion: No fourth question is sent.

statement: Evidence explanations do not expand into presenting disputed factual claims.
criterion: A conflicting outcome does not present the disputed claims as answers.

statement: smalltalk gets a bounded localized response with no KB call or unrestricted domain generation.
criterion: A smalltalk turn makes no KB call.

statement: conversation_meta answers only from authorized transcript material, labelled as conversation history.
criterion: Meta answers have empty sources and only message_refs.

statement: Common meta cases, such as the first user question, use deterministic transcript selection.
criterion: What was my first question returns sequence 1 without a model.

statement: A bounded LLM may phrase a meta answer when needed.
criterion: Any such LLM call is bounded and journaled.

statement: If the required history cannot be retrieved within bounds, the outcome is cannot_answer / history_unavailable.
criterion: That outcome is returned, with no fabricated history.

statement: out_of_scope yields localized cannot_answer / out_of_scope with no KB retrieval or general-knowledge fallback.
criterion: No KB or generation call.

statement: The Jev adapter validates answer names, primitive types, enum membership, finite 0..1 probabilities and distribution consistency.
criterion: Malformed responses are rejected.

statement: Missing or malformed decision output is DECISION_INVALID, not actionable uncertainty.
criterion: Malformed output yields 502 DECISION_INVALID.

statement: A Noul without a separate confidence field is valid.
criterion: Such a response is accepted.

statement: Any derived confidence metric carries its derivation and version label and is never presented as a provider-reported confidence.
criterion: Derived metrics are labelled.

statement: A live decision profile identifies an approved concrete returned model ID and rejects unapproved model drift before acting.
criterion: A drifted model ID causes rejection before the policy is applied.

statement: Where only a moving alias exists, an approved expected returned-ID set and a recorded limitation are required.
criterion: The profile lists approved IDs and the limitation.

statement: Model drift yields 503 MODEL_PROFILE_MISMATCH, an operational alert and no successful turn.
criterion: Drift returns 503, raises an alert and commits no turn.

statement: The Jev capability profile declares a verified or conservative input cap, its provenance and unknown operational behaviors.
criterion: The profile documents the cap, its source and the unknowns.

statement: An unanswered dispatch is uncertain unless evidence shows rejection or a recoverable result; a timeout does not prove delivery.
criterion: An unanswered Jev call ends uncertain.

statement: A second deterministic decision implementation passes the core conformance tests without a second paid provider.
criterion: The deterministic implementation passes the suite.

statement: Generation and summarization use application-owned input and output contracts independent of provider SDKs.
criterion: The core imports no LLM SDK.

statement: The pilot implements Anthropic Messages and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions as two distinct adapters with a shared conformance suite.
criterion: Both adapters pass the shared suite.

statement: Running the OpenAI-compatible model server is outside the product scope.
criterion: The repository contains no model server.

statement: Each (provider, endpoint, API version, model) profile declares limits, tokenizer or estimator, finish and refusal mapping, structured-output method, caching controls and usage semantics.
criterion: Profile validation requires every field.

statement: Unsupported mandatory capabilities fail configuration and are never silently ignored.
criterion: Startup fails on a missing mandatory capability.

statement: The generator receives the exact evidence set and policy chosen by the orchestrator and cannot override the chosen action.
criterion: The generator input equals the selected evidence, and the action is unchanged.

statement: The normalized generation result includes non-empty bounded text, referenced citation IDs, completion status and reported-or-unknown usage.
criterion: The result type carries each field.

statement: Free-form model text never supplies database operations, authorization decisions or arbitrary tools.
criterion: Model output triggers none of these.

statement: Hidden chain-of-thought is never requested or persisted as conversation content.
criterion: No reasoning content is stored.

statement: A grounded answer references only evidence supplied to that call and cites at least one item before commit.
criterion: An answer without a valid citation is not committed.

statement: An invalid, fabricated or missing required reference fails the turn with 502 CITATION_INVALID.
criterion: A fabricated citation returns 502 CITATION_INVALID.

statement: Source membership validation is not semantic entailment.
criterion: Documentation states the limitation.

statement: sources holds exactly the deduplicated cited subset in first-citation order.
criterion: sources equals the cited IDs, deduplicated and in order.

statement: A length-truncated answer fails with 502 GENERATION_TRUNCATED and is never committed.
criterion: Truncation returns 502, and no turn is committed.

statement: No hidden regeneration or continuation request is made by default.
criterion: Truncation triggers no second call.

statement: A known refusal is distinct from a transport or protocol failure.
criterion: A refusal maps to provider_refusal, not 5xx.

statement: A valid provider refusal produces cannot_answer / provider_refusal without a second provider or bypass attempt.
criterion: One call only, with a 200 provider_refusal outcome.

statement: A provider or model change rebuilds context from application state and revalidates limits without the previous provider's handles.
criterion: After a switch, the turn succeeds with no reuse of old handles.

statement: Generation context keeps the order: stable instructions, bounded summary, complete turns since the summary, current evidence, current question.
criterion: A golden test shows the ordered prompt structure.

statement: The unsummarized tail is append-only between checkpoints, not a sliding last-K window.
criterion: The prefix is unchanged between consecutive turns without a new checkpoint.

statement: Older content is compacted when thresholds are reached.
criterion: Compaction occurs at the threshold.

statement: Selective evidence and the new question come after reusable conversation segments.
criterion: Evidence and the question are at the prompt end.

statement: Stable formatting never justifies irrelevant text or exceeding a model window.
criterion: The prompt fits the window.

statement: Each decision, summary and generation call fits its role's independently configured input, output and byte budgets before dispatch.
criterion: Over-budget calls are not dispatched.

statement: Every call satisfies the window inequality.
criterion: estimated_input + reserved_output + safety_margin <= usable_window.

statement: For a byte-limited API, the byte cap is enforced too.
criterion: Over-byte calls are refused.

statement: Cached tokens count toward the context window.
criterion: The window check includes cached tokens.

statement: Jev's input cap is not inferred from the generation model.
criterion: Jev has its own configured cap.

statement: Summarization input is not assumed to fit because generation context does.
criterion: Summarizer calls are checked against their own budget.

statement: Startup validation checks that the maximum question, instructions, minimum context, output reserve and margin fit every role profile.
criterion: An infeasible profile fails startup.

statement: The service never silently truncates the current question or mandatory instructions to fit a call.
criterion: An oversize input yields an error, not truncation.

statement: When no tokenizer exists, the estimator declares a conservative method, byte guard and safety margin validated for the profile.
criterion: The profile declares each, and validation passes.

statement: The default safety reserve is the larger of a percentage of the usable window or a token floor.
criterion: max(10% of usable window, 256 tokens).

statement: A missing model limit is a configuration error, not permission for unbounded input.
criterion: Startup fails without a limit.

statement: Summary work triggers from role budgets and does not run on every message.
criterion: Short sessions make no summary calls.

statement: Each summary pass consumes a bounded forward chunk of unsummarized committed history and advances its monotonic coverage cursor, or fails explicitly.
criterion: Coverage increases after each successful pass.

statement: Summaries are size-bounded.
criterion: At most 4 KiB UTF-8 and within the consumers' tighter token budget.

statement: Summarizer calls per chat attempt are bounded by default.
criterion: At most 2 per attempt.

statement: A chunk plus previous summary, instructions and output allowance fits the summarizer's window.
criterion: Every summarizer call passes the window check.

statement: covered_seq is the last fully covered message, and an optional {message_seq, byte_offset} cursor records partial coverage.
criterion: The checkpoint stores both.

statement: Progress compares the pair monotonically, so partial coverage is never taken for a full turn.
criterion: A partial checkpoint does not advance covered_seq.

statement: The public transcript is unchanged by summarization.
criterion: Message history is identical before and after.

statement: Partial summary progress is durably checkpointed and reused when later steps fail.
criterion: After a generation failure, the retry reuses the checkpoint with no new summary of the same chunk.

statement: When more catch-up is needed beyond the per-attempt budget, CONTEXT_PREPARING is returned as retryable only if coverage advanced and further progress is possible.
criterion: CONTEXT_PREPARING only with advanced coverage.

statement: A context that cannot make bounded progress returns final 422 SESSION_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED.
criterion: Such a session returns 422, recorded as failed_final.

statement: An unresolved paid summary call still follows uncertain handling.
criterion: It is marked uncertain, not CONTEXT_PREPARING.

statement: A failed summary may be bypassed only when an existing safe context fits and the call outcome is known.
criterion: A bypass happens only under both conditions.

statement: Summary provenance distinguishes user statements, prior assistant assertions, cited KB facts, unresolved questions and preserved user constraints.
criterion: The summary structure labels each category.

statement: The implementation keeps summary coverage and source hashes and procedure and model versions so checkpoints can be validated after a restart or model change.
criterion: A checkpoint with a mismatched hash or version is rejected.

statement: Summary quality is measured, not asserted lossless.
criterion: A summary-quality evaluation is reported.

statement: Regeneration from original history stays possible when summary policy changes; checkpoints never rewrite history.
criterion: A policy change can rebuild the summaries.

statement: Native prompt caching is implemented for the selected LLM profiles, not just an unused interface.
criterion: Adapters send the cache controls.

statement: Answers, authorization and continuity are independent of cache hit, miss, eviction or restart.
criterion: Results are identical with the cache disabled or flushed.

statement: The cache contract distinguishes auto, prefer_reuse and no_explicit_cache from a separate hard require_no_prompt_cache constraint.
criterion: All four settings are modeled distinctly.

statement: no_explicit_cache adds no cache directives, though automatic provider caching may still happen.
criterion: No cache directives are sent.

statement: require_no_prompt_cache forbids cache reads and writes and is satisfiable only by a verified endpoint capability.
criterion: An unverified endpoint is rejected.

statement: A hard cache, retention or privacy constraint the endpoint cannot verify fails configuration before private content is sent.
criterion: Startup fails, and no content is sent.

statement: Cache retention, storage options and provider policy are explicitly configured or documented as immutable or unsupported.
criterion: Each profile declares these.

statement: Cacheable prompt segments serialize deterministically across requests and restarts for identical state and profile versions.
criterion: Byte-level golden tests are stable across restarts.

statement: Request IDs, timestamps and unstable ordering never enter reusable prompt prefixes unless semantically necessary.
criterion: Prefixes contain none of them.

statement: Prompt assembly uses ordered structures or deterministic serialization, checked by byte-level golden tests.
criterion: The golden tests pass.

statement: Adapters should place cache breakpoints after stable instructions, summary and the completed tail, keeping evidence and the question after them.
criterion: Breakpoint positions match in the adapter tests.

statement: Cross-session reuse is limited to non-private common instructions; session content never enters a shared application cache entry.
criterion: Shared entries hold no session content.

statement: Application cache identity includes authorization equivalence, tenant, profile and model and content versions, plus subject and session for private material.
criterion: Keys differ when any of these differ.

statement: Provider routing keys are not proof of tenant isolation.
criterion: Isolation is not claimed from routing keys.

statement: Private prefixes need a documented provider isolation boundary, and routing keys contain no raw personal identifiers.
criterion: Routing keys are opaque.

statement: The capability matrix pins and tests actual endpoint and model cache controls, thresholds, TTL semantics and usage accounting.
criterion: Each pinned profile has passing cache tests.

statement: Cache controls are not assumed present on every OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
criterion: Unverified endpoints get no cache controls.

statement: Hard no-cache support is never claimed from the absence of cache directives.
criterion: An unverified hard constraint is rejected.

statement: Optional pre-warming uses a declared capability, a bounded non-sensitive prefix and journaled usage, without blocking readiness or becoming a required background service.
criterion: Readiness is independent of warm-up, and its usage is journaled.

statement: Unsupported endpoints never receive invented parameters.
criterion: No unknown parameter is sent.

statement: Cache-write charges and uncertain warm-up outcomes are recorded even without generated text.
criterion: Warm-up usage records exist.

statement: Optional KB-result cache keys include query and context identity, authorization scope, filters and corpus revision, with an explicit TTL and invalidation policy.
criterion: A change in any part misses the cache.

statement: The KB cache is bypassed when freshness or authorization equivalence cannot be established.
criterion: In that case the KB is called directly.

statement: Optional cache failures degrade to uncached operation within the original resource and deadline limits.
criterion: With the cache down, turns succeed within the deadline.

statement: Complete-answer and semantic caching are not enabled in the pilot.
criterion: No such caching exists.

statement: Each inference attempt, including decisions, summaries, generation, retries and pre-warming, has a durable uniquely keyed usage record.
criterion: Every call has exactly one usage record.

statement: Usage records distinguish reported, estimated and unknown, and never turn missing usage or uncertain billing into zero.
criterion: Missing usage is stored as unknown.

statement: Usage normalization preserves provider field semantics and does not double-count cached input.
criterion: Cached input is counted once.

statement: Unsupported usage fields remain unknown.
criterion: They are stored as unknown.

statement: Operational provenance records configured and returned model IDs, endpoint profile, prompt, question and policy versions, summary coverage, KB revision and decision verdicts and probabilities.
criterion: The provenance record carries each field.

statement: Content-bearing provenance and saved stage outputs get access, encryption and deletion protections equal to conversation data.
criterion: They are covered by the same controls and the same deletion.

statement: Estimated cost uses a dated price profile and separately shows reported charges, estimates and unresolved possible charges.
criterion: The cost report has three separate figures and a price date.

statement: The service enforces per-attempt call and output budgets, including retries and summaries, before dispatching another paid operation.
criterion: An over-budget call is not dispatched.

statement: The default domain attempt has a fixed call budget.
criterion: 1 intent, 1 evidence assessment, at most 2 summaries, 1 generation.

statement: An opted-in uncertain retry adds a bounded number of calls per attempt.
criterion: At most 1 extra call per attempt.

statement: Shared endpoint and account rate limits still apply.
criterion: Retries respect the account limits.

statement: Real-price ceilings require complete price profiles; unknown pricing gives no false monetary guarantee.
criterion: A ceiling is refused without a complete price profile.

statement: Session deletion removes linked per-request content and provenance, keeping only approved non-content aggregates that cannot link back.
criterion: After deletion, no linked record remains.

statement: Aggregates may include date, provider and model, token totals and cost estimates, but exclude request, session and subject IDs, hashes and probability vectors.
criterion: Aggregate rows contain none of the excluded fields.

statement: Small or identifiable cohorts require aggregation or suppression under the retention policy.
criterion: Small cohorts are suppressed.

statement: Pseudonymous event rows are not treated as anonymous aggregates.
criterion: Such rows are deleted with the session.

statement: Every HTTP error uses RFC 9457 application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, instance, code, request_id, request_state and retryable as applicable.
criterion: Every error response validates against the problem schema.

statement: The problem type may be about:blank, with the stable application code giving the condition.
criterion: code is always present.

statement: retryable=true means a same-key retry may be allowed once the condition clears, never overriding auth, version or capacity checks.
criterion: Retries still go through every check.

statement: Retry-After is a bounded integer-second hint, not a promised completion time.
criterion: The value is a bounded integer.

statement: Error and status mapping follows the catalog, with uncertainty and commit reconciliation taking precedence over optimistic retry labels.
criterion: Each catalog code is produced in its case.

statement: 400 INVALID_REQUEST or UNSUPPORTED_LOCALE for invalid schema or field, with no claim.
criterion: No request record is created.

statement: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED for missing, invalid or expired identity, with no claim or a safe retryable pre-dispatch interruption.
criterion: No paid call follows.

statement: 403 RETRIEVAL_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN for an impermissible retrieval scope, with no paid call.
criterion: No paid call.

statement: 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for unknown, deleted or other-owner resources, indistinguishably.
criterion: The responses are identical.

statement: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT for the same key with different input; the existing record is unchanged.
criterion: The record is unchanged.

statement: 409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS for a queued, running or committing request, with Retry-After and status guidance.
criterion: Retry-After is present.

statement: 409 STATE_CONFLICT when the retry version changed, saved as failed_final.
criterion: The state is failed_final.

statement: 409 OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN for an unreconciled potentially charged dispatch, with no silent same-key execution.
criterion: No execution follows.

statement: 409 SESSION_BUSY when deletion races active or queued work; nothing is deleted.
criterion: The session is intact.

statement: 409 SESSION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED when authorization differs from the session snapshot; no history, replay or model access.
criterion: No data or calls.

statement: 413 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE for an oversized body, with no claim.
criterion: No request record is created.

statement: 422 CONTEXT_LIMIT or SESSION_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED when valid input cannot fit or progress, saved as failed_final.
criterion: The state is failed_final.

statement: 429 QUEUE_FULL, PRINCIPAL_LIMIT or ADMISSION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED before claim, with Retry-After; the same ID may be resubmitted.
criterion: No request record is created; a resubmission is accepted later.

statement: 502 KB_INVALID, DECISION_INVALID, GENERATION_INVALID, CITATION_INVALID or GENERATION_TRUNCATED for a known invalid upstream result, saved as failed_final, with no partial conversation.
criterion: No turn is committed.

statement: 503 KB_UNAVAILABLE, DECISION_UNAVAILABLE, LLM_UNAVAILABLE or UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMITED are retryable only with proven safe resume, otherwise OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN.
criterion: The classification follows the evidence.

statement: 503 STORE_UNAVAILABLE, WRITER_UNAVAILABLE or SERVICE_DRAINING means no admission or a safely journaled interruption; an unresolved commit is reconciled.
criterion: No guessed state.

statement: 503 MODEL_PROFILE_MISMATCH for unapproved model drift, with no successful turn.
criterion: No turn is committed.

statement: 503 CONTEXT_PREPARING when coverage advanced but more catch-up is needed, retryable only under the progress rule.
criterion: Coverage advanced.

statement: 504 QUEUE_TIMEOUT or START_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with no execution, stored retryable.
criterion: No paid call; the state is retryable.

statement: 504 DEPENDENCY_TIMEOUT or REQUEST_DEADLINE is retryable only before unresolved dispatch or with reusable results, otherwise OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN.
criterion: The classification follows the journal.

statement: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR is a safe generic problem, with request state following journal evidence.
criterion: No internal details are leaked.

statement: A client disconnect gets no invented HTTP delivery.
criterion: Nothing is sent after the disconnect.

statement: A disconnect's state and CLIENT_DISCONNECTED diagnostic appear in the journal and status response.
criterion: The status shows CLIENT_DISCONNECTED.

statement: A valid provider refusal is a 200 controlled outcome, not an infrastructure error.
criterion: A refusal returns 200.

statement: Same-key replay of a completed response or final problem preserves the original outcome and adds Idempotent-Replayed: true.
criterion: The replay body equals the original, with the header set.

statement: Every attempt has an absolute total deadline from handler entry, a pre-execution queue cap and a reserved finalization budget.
criterion: Total 180 s; queue 60 s; finalization reserve 5 s.

statement: Before each stage, the service verifies that the stage cap plus the remaining stages and finalization fit the remaining deadline.
criterion: A stage that cannot fit is not started.

statement: KB, decision, summary, generation, storage and capacity waits use cancellable bounded contexts derived from the absolute deadline.
criterion: Every wait is cancelled at the deadline.

statement: Default per-dependency time caps are set.
criterion: KB 10 s; each decision 10 s; each summary 25 s; generation 60 s; finalization 5 s.

statement: Dependency caps are limits within one absolute budget, not cumulative entitlements.
criterion: The sum is bounded by 180 s.

statement: A cold domain path with two summaries fits the total budget only when actual times permit, as decided by the start and stage guards.
criterion: The guards prevent exceeding 180 s.

statement: Caller cancellation removes waiting work and propagates to in-flight calls, without being taken as proof that provider work or billing was undone.
criterion: Cancellation stops the calls, and in-flight paid calls are marked uncertain.

statement: A detached finalization or reconciliation context may outlive the HTTP connection for a bounded time while keeping its slot until resolved.
criterion: At most 5 s beyond the disconnect.

statement: SDK backoff and retries respect remaining time, attempt limits, upstream retry hints and jitter, and never retry auth or schema errors.
criterion: There are no retries on 401 or 400, and retries stay within the deadline.

statement: Each dependency account has bounded in-flight and rate-limit controls shared across all roles using it.
criterion: Combined role traffic never exceeds the account limit.

statement: Intent, evidence, summary and generation calls cannot bypass the account limits through separate clients.
criterion: All roles share one limiter per account.

statement: Dependency limits are configurable independently of the 100-turn scheduler.
criterion: Changing one leaves the other unchanged.

statement: Gateway and load-balancer timeouts cover the service deadline plus finalization overrun and transport margin.
criterion: Pilot value 200 s.

statement: The HTTP server configures header-read, body-read and write timeouts for the deployment profile.
criterion: ReadHeaderTimeout 5 s; bounded body reads; WriteTimeout >= 200 s.

statement: Graceful shutdown stops admission, fails readiness, removes queued work safely and drains active work before releasing writer ownership.
criterion: Drain at most 185 s.

statement: Deployment termination grace covers pre-stop work, drain and a safety margin.
criterion: Grace 200 s with pre-stop <= 5 s.

statement: Network calls carrying private content use authenticated encrypted transport to allowlisted endpoints, except isolated local tests.
criterion: Non-TLS or non-allowlisted endpoints are refused outside tests.

statement: Secrets come through approved runtime secret mechanisms and never enter Git, prompts, responses, fixtures or logs.
criterion: A secret scan finds none.

statement: Conversation and content-bearing journal storage use approved at-rest encryption and restricted access.
criterion: The storage configuration shows encryption and access limits.

statement: Logs and metrics exclude raw tokens, full transcripts, KB passages and sensitive prompt content by default.
criterion: Captured logs and metrics contain none of them.

statement: Input, output, journal and diagnostic handling enforces byte and count limits and sanitizes untrusted source metadata without fetching source URLs.
criterion: Oversized or malicious metadata is bounded and sanitized, and no fetch occurs.

statement: A citation URL is KB-supplied provenance, not permission for server-side fetching.
criterion: Citation URLs are never fetched.

statement: The session stores an authorization fingerprint of owner, normalized roles, retrieval scope and authorization revision.
criterion: The fingerprint changes when any of them changes.

statement: A changed fingerprint blocks history, replay and context reuse with SESSION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED but still allows authorized deletion.
criterion: Reads return 409, and DELETE succeeds.

statement: A deployment documents whether historical answers are snapshots of formerly authorized evidence or need current document-level reauthorization.
criterion: The deployment profile records the choice.

statement: The pilot does not implement retroactive document-level redaction of historical answers, summaries and replays.
criterion: The limitation is documented.

statement: Blocking changed roles or revisions catches only signalled changes, not unexposed ACL changes.
criterion: The limitation is documented.

statement: Sensitive production use needs reliable revision propagation or an approved historical-access policy, not reliance on fresh retrieval.
criterion: One of the two exists before sensitive use.

statement: A release needing immediate historical revocation stays blocked until the identity and KB contract can enforce it.
criterion: Such a release is marked blocked.

statement: Before real personal data is enabled, the deployment has an approved data-classification and processor inventory covering every provider.
criterion: The approved inventory exists before real data.

statement: The inventory records data categories, purposes, locations, subprocessors, retention, training-use terms and permitted classification.
criterion: The inventory has each field per provider.

statement: The privacy or legal owner approves the processing and international-transfer basis, including KVKK Article 9 and GDPR Chapter V, before transfers are enabled.
criterion: Approval is recorded before transfers.

statement: The deployment profile separately verifies prompt-cache behavior, app-state storage and provider logging and retention, not equating store=false with zero retention.
criterion: Each is verified separately.

statement: Each provider needs its own documented retention evidence; TypeSafe retention is not inferred from other terms.
criterion: Jev has its own evidence.

statement: When a required location or retention property is unknown, real-data activation fails closed, while synthetic tests stay available.
criterion: Real-data mode refuses to start.

statement: Session deletion uses the same per-session lifecycle and admission synchronization as request creation and execution.
criterion: Delete and admit serialize per session.

statement: Deletion returns 409 SESSION_BUSY while any active, queued, committing or reserved work exists for the session.
criterion: DELETE during work returns 409.

statement: Deleting an inactive session first tombstones it atomically, so admission, summaries and commits cannot resurrect it.
criterion: After a tombstone, concurrent writes fail.

statement: A 204 deletion removes transcript, summaries, metadata, request results and linked content-bearing records, and invalidates local caches.
criterion: No linked content remains.

statement: If purge fails after tombstoning, the session stays unavailable for chat and reads.
criterion: Reads return 404.

statement: A repeated authorized DELETE or startup purge recovery finishes cleanup without reactivating the session.
criterion: The session stays deleted.

statement: Backup expiry and provider-side deletion are separate documented controls, not implied by a live-store 204.
criterion: Documentation states these controls.

statement: Session IDs are server-generated cryptographically random UUIDs checked against a durable reserved-ID registry before allocation.
criterion: A reserved ID is never allocated.

statement: The registry keeps a protected digest of allocated and deleted IDs, so non-reuse does not rest on collision probability alone.
criterion: Digests persist after deletion.

statement: The registry holds no conversation, owner or content fields after purge.
criterion: Registry rows have only the digest and status.

statement: Digest key or version migration keeps the non-reuse checks.
criterion: Old IDs are still refused after migration.

statement: The anti-reuse record belongs in the data inventory, and hashing is not claimed to anonymize data.
criterion: The inventory lists the registry.

statement: Retention cleanup uses the same busy checks and tombstone and purge semantics as explicit deletion.
criterion: Retention cleanup on a busy session is deferred.

statement: Real-data deployment configures inactivity retention, backup retention, deletion processing and legal exceptions before readiness allows real data.
criterion: Readiness fails without them.

statement: The synthetic pilot may disable automatic expiry; no production retention period is fabricated.
criterion: No invented period exists.

statement: Status polling and duplicate replays do not extend retention unless the policy says so.
criterion: Polling leaves the expiry unchanged.

statement: Startup recovery finishes interrupted tombstone purges without restoring removed request keys or leaking deleted content into summaries or model calls.
criterion: After a crash mid-purge, the restart completes the purge with no leak.
