statement: Content and status reads after tombstoning return 404, with authorized DELETE recovery handled separately.
criterion: Reads return 404, and DELETE can complete.

statement: The service implements the named configuration defaults and validates their combined consistency at startup.
criterion: Inconsistent defaults fail startup.

statement: The repository and process name is chat-orchestrator.
criterion: The name matches.

statement: One intended active writer, enforced by PostgreSQL ownership and epoch fencing.
criterion: 1 writer.

statement: max_active_requests default.
max_queued_requests default, including same-session waits.
max_queued_per_session default.
Per-principal active and queued defaults.
criterion: 10 active / 10 queued.

statement: Session creation rate and retained sessions per principal.
criterion: 30/min, burst 10 / 1,000 retained.

statement: Queue wait and request deadline defaults.
Minimum start budget and finalization budget defaults.
Cold admission duration estimate, updated conservatively from observation.
criterion: 30 s per turn.

statement: Dependency caps.
criterion: KB 10 s; each decision 10 s; each summary 25 s; generation 60 s.

statement: max_summary_calls_per_attempt default.
max_uncertain_model_retries default and permitted values.
criterion: Default 0; allowed 0 or 1.

statement: HTTP body, question and chat-response limits.
criterion: 32 KiB / 8 KiB / 64 KiB.

statement: Maximum normalized KB items, with evidence bytes and tokens profile-bounded.
criterion: 8 items.

statement: Summary text limit, with the tighter role token cap applied.
criterion: 4 KiB.

statement: History page size.
criterion: 50 default; 100 maximum.

statement: Supported locales are tr-TR and en-US, with tr-TR the default.
criterion: Only these two are accepted, and the default is tr-TR.

statement: Gateway and server write timeouts.
criterion: Gateway 200 s; server write >= 200 s.

statement: Header and body read timeouts.
criterion: Header 5 s; body bounded to 10 s.

statement: Drain and termination grace.
criterion: Drain 185 s; grace 200 s; pre-stop <= 5 s.

statement: Native cache intent defaults to prefer_reuse, subject to the approved privacy and capability profile.
criterion: The default is prefer_reuse.

statement: Pre-warm is disabled, the generic KB cache is optional and disabled, and the full-response cache is deferred.
criterion: All are off by default.

statement: Live external tests are opt-in and separate from Gate A.
criterion: Gate A runs no live test.

statement: Production retention and prices need explicit approved configuration; no legal period or current price is assumed.
criterion: No default retention or price exists.

statement: Raising any limit requires revalidating queue delay, provider quotas, DB connections, memory, the HTTP timeout chain and model budgets.
criterion: The revalidation is documented with any change.

statement: The 100-concurrency test uses enough distinct principals to respect the principal cap, unless a single-principal test explicitly overrides the cap.
criterion: The test uses at least 10 principals or an explicit override.

statement: Provider endpoints, credentials, model profiles, protocol versions, limits, policies and storage settings are configuration artifacts, not business-logic constants.
criterion: No such value is hard-coded in core logic.

statement: Startup rejects incompatible deadlines, missing model caps, invalid threshold orderings, unknown mandatory capabilities and incomplete non-synthetic privacy or auth profiles.
criterion: Each case fails startup.

statement: Toolchain, dependencies, database image and fixture versions are pinned in reproducible artifacts, with no unpinned downloads during the gate.
criterion: The gate runs with pinned artifacts only.

statement: Structured lifecycle logs make request and attempt state, admission sequence, version, writer epoch, stage timing, action and error category diagnosable without raw content.
criterion: Log entries carry these fields and no content.

statement: Metrics cover active and waiting work, rejections, queue delay, principal saturation, rate limits, summary progress, retries, usage uncertainty and cache reads and writes, with bounded-cardinality labels.
criterion: Each metric is exported.

statement: Request, session and subject IDs are never metric label values.
criterion: No such label exists.

statement: Readiness requires valid configuration, a usable store, current writer ownership and completed recovery, without paid calls on probes.
criterion: Readiness fails when any is missing, and probes make no model call.

statement: Transient queue saturation produces admission errors and metrics without making the whole service unready.
criterion: A full queue returns 429 while readiness stays up.

statement: A dependency or model-drift alert identifies the affected endpoint or profile without exposing keys or private prompts.
criterion: The alert names the profile and carries no secret.

statement: Gate A runs without outbound internet, production credentials or hidden paid calls, allowing loopback infrastructure only.
criterion: Gate A passes with the network blocked.

statement: Core tests use deterministic fakes, protocol tests use local HTTP fixtures, and persistence and ownership tests use real local PostgreSQL.
criterion: The test suites use those dependencies.

statement: Concurrency and timeout tests use barriers, observable states and controlled clocks rather than relying only on sleeps.
criterion: These tests are not timing-flaky.

statement: Gate preparation supplies vendored modules, a pinned Go toolchain, cgo, a C compiler and a preloaded PostgreSQL image or instance.
criterion: All are present before the gate.

statement: Provisioning may use the network before the offline boundary, but gate execution never pulls modules or images.
criterion: No pull occurs during the gate.

statement: go mod vendor is the dependency preparation path unless a documented sealed alternative is tested.
criterion: vendor/ is used.

statement: The gate includes formatting, compilation, go vet, unit, contract, store and e2e tests and race detection, with failures propagated to the exit status.
criterion: Any failure gives a non-zero exit.

statement: The gate script runs offline with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, GOSUMDB=off, -mod=vendor and CGO_ENABLED=1, checking gofmt, build, vet, test and test -race.
criterion: The script runs as given and exits 0.

statement: The formatting check covers tracked generated Go files but not vendored code.
criterion: gofmt excludes vendor/.

statement: Missing prerequisites or skipped mandatory tests fail; neither counts as a pass.
criterion: Skips cause a failure.

statement: The implementation satisfies every applicable acceptance family, with named subtests per normative requirement.
criterion: Each family A01 to A38 passes, with named subtests.

statement: A01: a normal domain turn does history load, intent, authorized KB, three decisions, generation, citation validation and one atomic commit.
criterion: A01 passes.

statement: A02: a restart preserves transcript and version, a follow-up uses the prior referent, and a cold cache does not change continuity.
criterion: A02 passes.

statement: A03: budgeted checkpoints preserve transcript, coverage and provenance; generation failure keeps paid summary progress.
criterion: A03 passes.

statement: A04: a barrier test reaches 100 active sessions, never 101; the 101st starts after release; idle sessions use no slots.
criterion: A04 passes.

statement: A05: FIFO within sessions, no cross-session blocking, tail reinsertion and principal-cap skipping.
criterion: A05 passes.

statement: A06: queue bounds, estimated-start rejection, start guard and expiry, with no claim on overload and no call for cancelled waiters.
criterion: A06 passes.

statement: A07: concurrent same-key claims, completed replay, changed-payload conflict, fingerprint and retained keys.
criterion: A07 passes.

statement: A08: crashes at each dispatch stage recover from evidence, never silently replaying an uncertain call.
criterion: A08 passes.

statement: A09: atomic commit, version collision, lost acknowledgement and reconciliation without regeneration.
criterion: A09 passes.

statement: A10: every policy row, contradictory judgments, empty evidence, exact probability boundaries and malformed-decision precedence.
criterion: A10 passes.

statement: A11: Jev wire mapping, required model, validation, Noul without confidence, labelled metrics and model drift.
criterion: A11 passes.

statement: A12: both LLM adapters pass shared conformance, and unsupported capabilities fail without core changes.
criterion: A12 passes.

statement: A13: cache request mapping, byte-identical prefix across restarts, partial invalidation, misses and expiry, and pre-warm limits.
criterion: A13 passes.

statement: A14: durable usage for every call type, provider-specific cache accounting and unknown usage.
criterion: A14 passes.

statement: A15: bulkheads, 429s, retry limits, cancellation, deadlines and resource release at every stage.
criterion: A15 passes.

statement: A16: JWT validation and renewal, owner separation, 404 indistinguishability and authorization-change blocking.
criterion: A16 passes.

statement: A17: pagination, cursor scope, busy DELETE 409, deletion races, purge recovery and ID non-reuse.
criterion: A17 passes.

statement: A18: two-process startup, recovery isolation, lock loss, stale epoch, the control-row race and no non-owner model call.
criterion: A18 passes.

statement: A19: real PostgreSQL migrations, conformance, restart persistence, transaction failure and a backup and restore drill.
criterion: A19 passes.

statement: A20: the offline gate from prepared dependencies fails on missing prerequisites, with no hidden skips, network access or committed credentials.
criterion: A20 passes.

statement: A21: OpenAPI and error-envelope compliance across all error statuses, size bounds, saved problems and replay headers.
criterion: A21 passes.

statement: A22: pre-dispatch cancellation retries with the same ID, the version guard rejects a stale retry, and a first-attempt FIFO is not rejected.
criterion: A22 passes.

statement: A23: uncertain retry 0 or 1, no retry after disconnect or restart, one extra call, identity checks and the duplicate-charge ledger.
criterion: A23 passes.

statement: A24: an oversized backlog catches up durably in chunks, same-key continuation succeeds, and no progress returns a terminal error.
criterion: A24 passes.

statement: A25: smalltalk skips the KB, meta answers use the transcript, and out-of-scope and ambiguous intent are controlled.
criterion: A25 passes.

statement: A26: fabricated or missing citations, cited-subset order, wrong-session refs, empty output, truncation and refusal mapping.
criterion: A26 passes.

statement: A27: a Turkish response from English evidence, locale precedence, immutable defaults and filter narrowing.
criterion: A27 passes.

statement: A28: timeout alignment, disconnected-commit reconciliation, the readiness, drain and termination chain, and forced-shutdown recovery.
criterion: A28 passes.

statement: A29: a hard no-cache or no-retention incompatibility fails before dispatch, plus synthetic versus real-data activation checks.
criterion: A29 passes.

statement: A30: startup validation for all roles, cache tokens counted and no silent truncation after a model switch.
criterion: A30 passes.

statement: A31: one subject cannot exhaust the slots, plus per-principal quotas and bounded bookkeeping.
criterion: A31 passes.

statement: A32: deletion removes usage and provenance, non-linkable aggregates survive, logs are redacted and metric labels bounded.
criterion: A32 passes.

statement: A33: a missing KB or identity contract blocks Gate A, and missing credentials block live gates without fake success.
criterion: A33 passes.

statement: A34: each claimed live cache profile records a provider-reported positive cache read, or stays unverified.
criterion: At least 1 positive cache read per claimed profile.

statement: A35: quality harness, frozen labelled set, baseline, reports and release thresholds.
criterion: A35 passes.

statement: A36: complete requirement-to-test mapping, pins, delivery evidence and bootstrap separation.
criterion: A36 passes.

statement: A37: untrusted instructions cannot alter endpoint, owner or policy or execute tools; live behavior is measured in Gate C.
criterion: A37 passes.

statement: A38: a provider or model change rebuilds context, validates checkpoints and cache identity, respects budgets and uses no old handle.
criterion: A38 passes.

statement: The repository maintains docs/tests/traceability.json with one entry per normative requirement ID, listing acceptance IDs, test names, evidence paths and status.
criterion: Every requirement ID has one entry.

statement: traceability.json follows the illustrated shape: document_id, revision and requirements entries.
criterion: The file validates against that shape.

statement: CI rejects duplicate or unknown IDs, unmapped requirements, missing mandatory test names and evidence marking an unexecuted or skipped test as passed.
criterion: Each defect fails CI.

statement: Live-gate statuses distinguish passed, failed, blocked and unverified from planned.
criterion: The status field allows exactly these five values.

statement: Quality thresholds and assertions are versioned before evaluation and never weakened after failures without a reviewed baseline change.
criterion: The threshold history shows versioning before evaluation.

statement: The project keeps calibration and held-out synthetic evaluation sets with reviewed labels and fixed evidence.
criterion: >= 20 calibration and >= 40 held-out cases.

statement: The held-out set has a fixed composition by category.
criterion: >= 16 answerable (>= 8 follow-ups), 12 non-answerable, 4 clarification, 4 meta, 2 smalltalk, 2 out-of-scope.

statement: The held-out set includes adversarial overlays and both languages.
criterion: >= 8 adversarial cases; >= 12 each in Turkish and English.

statement: The held-out set exercises summarization and preserved user constraints.
criterion: >= 4 session sequences.

statement: Every case states expected action, answerability, allowed references, required facts, forbidden claims and expected locale.
criterion: Each case has all six fields.

statement: Gate C uses the real Jev and LLM profiles, fixed prompt and policy versions and frozen KB evidence, not fakes.
criterion: The Gate C configuration uses no fake.

statement: Using a KB fixture in Gate C is recorded and does not certify real retrieval quality.
criterion: The report records the fixture choice.

statement: The held-out set runs twice per release profile, keeping every response and error and reporting per-run and aggregate counts.
criterion: Two runs are reported in full.

statement: Each run meets the release floors, with errors counted as failures in the denominators.
criterion: Every floor is met in both runs.

statement: Answer rate on labelled answerable domain cases.
Correct domain abstention on missing, conflicting or insufficient cases.
criterion: >= 95%; zero unsupported consequential claims in the critical subset.

statement: Citation identifier validity on returned domain answers.
Supported factual claims among generated domain claims.
criterion: >= 95%, with numerator, denominator and rubric.

statement: Correct intent and action on clarification, meta, smalltalk and out-of-scope cases.
criterion: >= 90% aggregate, with per-category results.

statement: Conversation facts and constraints preserved through summary.
criterion: >= 90% overall; 100% of critical constraints.

statement: Requested response language.
criterion: >= 95% for generated text; 100% for templates.

statement: The release floors are pilot targets, not statistical guarantees.
criterion: The report states this.

statement: Small denominators and raw failures stay visible.
criterion: The report shows the denominators and failures.

statement: Groundedness and summary-fidelity scoring has a documented human-review rubric or audited assessor, with human review of every critical failure and disputed score.
criterion: The rubric exists, and each critical or disputed item has a review.

statement: The quality report shows abstention, answerable-case errors, threshold behavior, latency, usage and unresolved cost alongside the scores.
criterion: The report has each section.

statement: A change in decision model, threshold, core prompt, summary policy or generation model triggers the relevant quality regression before promotion.
criterion: Promotion is blocked until the regression passes.

statement: The integration plan closes the interface inputs before claiming the affected implementation and full Gate A complete.
criterion: Each input is closed or Gate A is not claimed.

statement: The KB wire contract (method, path, schemas, auth, mapping, limits, revision, failure and billing semantics) must be supplied; it is not yet in the source material.
criterion: An approved KB contract exists.

statement: Principal transport: confirm issuer or gateway claim compatibility with the RS256 profile, or approve a mapping, using local signed fixtures.
criterion: Compatibility is confirmed or a mapping approved.

statement: Storage: pin the PostgreSQL version and image, schema and migrations, and the advisory-lock and fencing profile.
criterion: The pins are recorded.

statement: LLM protocols: pin protocol fixtures and capability schemas for both selected adapters.
criterion: The fixtures are pinned.

statement: Decision input budgets: select a conservative local test cap and estimator, and record missing provider ceilings.
criterion: The cap and gaps are recorded.

statement: Public API and KB authorization policy: freeze the metadata and filter mapping, historical-access policy and any required authorization revision.
criterion: The policy is frozen.

statement: An invented KB endpoint, an incompatible JWT assumption or an untested remote-store transaction does not count as closure.
criterion: No such substitute is accepted.

statement: Gate B, Gate C and real-data activation stay blocked or unverified for any missing input.
criterion: A missing input gives a blocked or unverified status.

statement: Actual KB location and access: endpoint, corpus, credentials, safe test content and protocol acceptance.
criterion: All are supplied before Gate B.

statement: Jev account and model: credential delivery, concrete returned model, alias mapping, observed limits and policy profile.
criterion: All are supplied before Gate B.

statement: Generation and summary models: real endpoint and model IDs, capability and retention evidence, price profile and test authorization.
criterion: All are supplied before Gate B.

statement: A second local or hosted LLM integration needs a provisioned endpoint only when live support is claimed.
criterion: Offline protocol tests need no endpoint.

statement: Production identity and storage: issuer keys or gateway mapping, DB connection and secrets, and the writer and deploy profile.
criterion: All are supplied before production.

statement: Privacy and retention: data categories, approved processors, locations and transfers, retention and the historical-access decision.
criterion: All are supplied before real data.

statement: Native caching evidence: a script above the cache minimum, repeated within the lifetime, with reported read evidence.
criterion: The evidence exists for each claimed profile.

statement: Unknown credentials, limits, prices, URLs or model IDs are never replaced with fabricated values or claimed live success.
criterion: No fabricated value is present.

statement: The repository name is fixed as chat-orchestrator; the GitHub owner and brief location are bootstrap inputs, not runtime configuration.
criterion: Runtime configuration contains no owner or location.

statement: Delivery includes source, migrations, adapters, OpenAPI and wire contracts, configuration examples, operational and privacy profiles, fixtures, quality fixtures, traceability and gate scripts.
criterion: Each artifact is present.

statement: Gate A passes all deterministic software, configuration and contract tests with real local PostgreSQL and offline dependencies.
criterion: The Gate A run passes offline.

statement: Gate B separately exercises the actual KB, the pinned Jev profile and at least one real LLM, with sanitized reproducible evidence.
criterion: >= 1 real LLM, plus the real KB and Jev.

statement: A live native-cache claim includes a provider-reported positive cache read from a scripted repeated-prefix case.
criterion: >= 1 positive cache read, otherwise unverified.

statement: An expired or too-short prompt is not valid cache proof.
criterion: Such runs are not counted.

statement: A no-hit run may pass core integration but not caching.
criterion: Caching stays unverified.

statement: Each adapter's live status is recorded independently; fake-backed tests are not real-account access.
criterion: Statuses are recorded per adapter.

statement: Gate C meets the frozen quality thresholds before a model and policy profile is presented as product-ready.
criterion: All thresholds are met.

statement: Bootstrap verification and external gate execution are reported separately from product completeness and live acceptance.
criterion: The report has separate sections.

statement: Bootstrap templates and fact and answer records are validated in their own workflow, not invented in the product specification.
criterion: They are validated in that workflow.

statement: The service is never marked fully complete while required contracts, durability or safety tests, live cache evidence or quality gates are blocked, failed or unverified.
criterion: The completion status reflects every gate.

statement: The release package identifies source, configuration and model profiles, Gate A/B/C outcomes, deployment limitations and evidence locations.
criterion: The package lists each.

statement: The release distinguishes an implemented adapter, a verified live integration and an approved data-processing deployment.
criterion: The three are reported separately.

statement: Tested provider versions are pinned because provider behavior can change.
criterion: The versions are pinned in configuration.
